scope.description: Hand-researched deepening tranche for Japanese numbered P Promotional cards, emphasizing the numbered 001/P-047/P promo spine, route-specific distribution memory, and high-gravity rows where mascot, legend, campaign, food, travel, tournament, and fan-club culture can easily collapse into generic promo language.
not_claiming: illustrator authority where the source row does not provide it

sources.title: Local Japanese promo WotC catalog: P Promotional cards
Bulbapedia raw wikitext: P Promotional cards (TCG)

claims.text: The local catalog models P Promotional cards as a numbered Japanese promo release beginning July 2001 and running through 2002.
The local release and boundary proof model 47 numbered P Promotional rows, 001/P through 047/P, from the selected raw setlist.

The local rows show P Promotional as a distribution web rather than one product: movie tie-ins, Pokemon Card Trainers inserts, CoroCoro, ANA, Nintendo Spaceworld, Tropical Mega Battle, Starter Triple Get Campaign, Pokemon Fan Club, Pokemon Center commemorations, McDonald's, Battle Road, Pokemon Festa, and Happy Adventure Rally all appear in the modeled page.

This tranche deepens the rows most likely to pull collector and agent attention: ANA Pikachu 004/P, Tropical Wind 008/P, Ho-Oh 010/P, Starter Triple Get Venusaur 012/P, Blastoise 013/P, Charizard 014/P, Shining Imakuni? 018/P, McDonald's Pikachu 021/P, McDonald's Umbreon 025/P, McDonald's Mew 033/P, and Happy Adventure Rally Lugia 047/P.

The selected raw P Promotional source rows do not provide illustrator names for this slice. The history layer preserves that silence rather than importing regular-card artist memory into a route-specific promo row.

P Promotional cards matter because they show Pokemon's early-2000s assembly as a social machine: airlines, magazines, tournaments, fast food counters, fan clubs, movie releases, city stores, and rallies all become card routes. The printed NNN/P number is the thin line that keeps that social route from dissolving into generic promo fog.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Confirm the printed NNN/P number and distribution route before treating a famous character as the target P Promotional row.
steps: Read the printed promo number and match it to the exact NNN/P row.
Preserve the distribution route, such as ANA, CoroCoro, McDonald's, Starter Triple Get, Tropical Mega Battle, Fan Club, or Happy Adventure Rally.
Do not collapse multiple P Promotional cards with the same Pokemon name into one want or seller response.
Do not borrow illustrator authority, rarity, price, or physical authenticity from a regular expansion print.
Ask for row-number evidence if the card is being used transactionally.

narrative.human_title: P Promotional cards: the numbered spine of a social machine
narrative.why_it_matters: P Promotional is not one vibe. It is Pokemon learning to move through everyday Japanese life: a plane campaign, a comic insert, a movie ticket, a fast-food weekend, a fan-club welcome, a tournament table, a summer rally. The collector romance is in the route. The protocol lesson is simple and severe: the name is not enough; the number and route have to come with it.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Venusaur as numbered P Promotional row 012/P in the Starter Triple Get Campaign Red Green Course.
Bulbapedia identifies the underlying card as Venusaur / フシギバナ Fushigibana, a Grass Stage 2 Pokemon with HP 100, Fire weakness, retreat cost 2, and Atsuko Nishida illustration credit.
Bulbapedia places this card in a lineage that includes English Expedition Base Set, Japanese Pokemon-e Starter Deck 004/029, and Japanese P Promotional 012/P.
Bulbapedia describes the P Promotional 012/P print as a Cosmos Holofoil reprint available through the Starter Triple Get Campaign Red Green Course.

Bulbapedia describes the Starter Triple Get Campaign as a proof-of-purchase-seal postcard lottery: entrants collected three seals from Pokemon-e Starter Decks, and lottery drawings distributed Red Green Course sets containing Venusaur 012/P, Blastoise 013/P, and Charizard 014/P, alongside a separate Gold Silver Course for Johto starters.
The card carries Leech Seed / やどりぎのたね and Fury Strikes / みだれうち, plus e-Reader data; the e-Reader note separates the non-holo and holo card IDs and says there is no long strip for this card.
Atsuko Nishida's Venusaur matters here because her Expedition-era art is being moved through a Japanese promo redemption apparatus; the image is familiar, but the route is not a booster-pack route.

Agents should distinguish Venusaur 012/P from Expedition Base Set 67/165, Japanese Pokemon-e Starter Deck 004/029, Base/No Rarity Venusaur, Trade Please Venusaur, and other Venusaur promos; the P number and Starter Triple Get route are load-bearing.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Pikachu as numbered P Promotional row 021/P in the McDonald's promotion held on Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays from January 26 through February 24, 2002.
Bulbapedia identifies the underlying card as Pikachu / ピカチュウ, a Lightning Basic Pokemon with HP 50, Fighting weakness, retreat cost 1, and Atsuko Nishida illustration credit.
Bulbapedia places this card in a lineage that includes the Sample Set, English Expedition Base Set 124/165, Japanese Base Expansion Pack 016/128, and Japanese P Promotional 021/P.
Bulbapedia says the P Promotional print used new artwork by Atsuko Nishida and was released through a McDonald's promotion running between January 26 and February 24, 2002.
The card carries Lightning Tail / でんきしっぽ and Tackle / たいあたり, and its e-Reader long strip contains sound data for the Construction: Melody Box application.

Bulbapedia separates three print contexts: standard Expedition and P Promotional prints with card ID B-16-#, and a Sample version with card ID M-16-# used to demonstrate Dot Code technology before Expedition's release.

Pikachu 021/P matters because it moves the mascot through an ordinary weekend ritual: a McDonald's promotion, public holidays, e-Reader sound data, and a numbered P-promo spine all wrapped around a new Nishida Pikachu image.

Agents should distinguish Pikachu 021/P from Expedition Base Set 124/165, Japanese Base Expansion Pack 016/128, Sample Set Pikachu, other McDonald's Pikachu cards, ANA Pikachu 004/P, Festa Pikachu 038/P, Happy Adventure Rally Pikachu 044/P, and generic Pikachu promos; the P number and McDonald's date window are load-bearing.

The protocol lesson is the same as the collector joy: route makes the mascot real.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Pikachu as numbered P Promotional row 038/P, distributed as a Pokemon Festa 2002 orienteering commemoration prize.
Bulbapedia identifies the card as Pikachu / ピカチュウ, a Lightning Basic Pokemon with HP 40, Fighting weakness, retreat cost 1, and Midori Harada illustration credit.

Bulbapedia says the 038/P print was first available as an orienteering commemorative card at Battle Festa 2002 venues in Japan between July and August 2002; people who collected at least three stamps by visiting different events at each venue were given the card.

Bulbapedia lists Battle Festa 2002 venues for this route: Sapporo Community Dome, Tokyo International Exhibition Center, Port Messe Nagoya, Intex Osaka, and West Japan General Exhibition Center in Fukuoka, with some coinciding with Battle Road Summer 2002 tournaments.
The card carries Smash Link / スマッシュリンク, an attack that references Super Smash Bros. Melee through its Mewtwo Bench condition.

Bulbapedia links 038/P and 044/P as two P Promotional prints with slightly different Midori Harada artwork: 038/P has card ID Z-26-a and a self-contained Pikachu mini-game in the long strip, while 044/P has card ID Z-26-b and a Tokotoko Truck mini-game requiring four other P Promotional cards.

Pikachu 038/P matters because it turns a card into a record of movement: walk the venue, collect stamps, touch multiple event points, and the mascot becomes a prize for having physically traversed the Pokemon Festa apparatus.

Agents should distinguish Pikachu 038/P from the paired 044/P Happy Adventure Rally print, McDonald's Pikachu 021/P, ANA Pikachu 004/P, other P Promotional Pikachu rows, and generic e-Reader Pikachu cards; the 038/P number, Battle Festa route, and Z-26-a e-Reader ID are load-bearing.
